findings.issue: A CTE that shadows a real table drops that table's access row. The filter `kw !== 'table' && ctes.has(table.toLowerCase())` applies to every FROM/JOIN in the statement, including the one inside the CTE's own body. In `WITH orders AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE open) SELECT ... FROM orders` the inner FROM orders reads the real table, but both refs are dropped, so merge.mjs makes no entity or access row for it. Shadowing a table with a filtered CTE of the same name is a common pattern in the analytics SQL this task targets. py15 only covers a CTE-named table in another statement. Judged from reading; I did not run it.
findings.resolution: Keep a ref to a CTE name when it sits inside that CTE's own definition parentheses (or when the name has no earlier CTE definition ending before the ref). At minimum record the shadowing case in the sqlStatements comment and add a py15 case for it.

findings.issue: privateDir is applied to the shared parent <tmpdir>/archmap as well as the per-repo directory. On a multi-user host where tmpdir is /tmp, the first user to run plan owns /tmp/archmap at 0o700, and every other user's plan then exits 2 with 'not owned by the current user'. The remedy the message offers, `--work <dir>`, is the one SKILL.md forbids (subagents can only write under the project or the OS temp dir). R11 asked to refuse a foreign-owned directory, but not to lock the other users out of the default.
findings.resolution: Give the first level a per-user name (<tmpdir>/archmap-<uid>/<hash>, or fall back to fs.mkdtempSync under the tmpdir) so the parent is never shared. Keep the lstat/owner checks on that name.

findings.issue: `python3 -I` also drops the per-user site directory (it implies -s), not only the cwd and PYTHON* variables. A duckdb installed with `pip install --user` was importable by the old call and now is not, and readerFor reports 'the python duckdb module is not installed', which is wrong. The isolation is right for rule 7; the false reason is the cost. Judged from reading.
findings.resolution: Make the skip reason name the isolated-mode limit (duckdb must be in the interpreter's own or a virtualenv's site-packages), or keep -I and also check `python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.flags.isolated)'` is not needed. Add the sentence to the reason string.

findings.issue: The post-dispatch check says to run `git status --porcelain` with plan and again after every dispatch, and that it 'must not change'. finish and render write architecture.model.json, the layout and the HTML into <out>, which is docs/architecture inside the repository by default. After the synthesizer or reviewer dispatch the status therefore differs from plan's, and read literally the orchestrator is told to stop and report a write outside the agent's path on a normal build. The baseline for 'must not change' is not named.
findings.resolution: Name the baseline: compare with the status printed by the driver step that ran immediately before the dispatch (explorers: plan's; synthesizer: finish's; reviewer: render's). Extend s16 to pin that sentence.

findings.issue: The diff changes `const cv = call.args[2]` to `const cv =call.args[2]` (space lost) on a line the task did not need to touch. It is harmless but a stray edit in a file the task owns.
